content.text:
Perfect! I now have all the information I need. The issue is clear:

1. The ledger-export job has `activeDeadlineSeconds: 3600` (1 hour)
2. The actual job is taking ~2 hours (from 01:00 to 02:00+ for 69/95 batches)
3. When it hits the 1-hour deadline, Kubernetes terminates it with `DeadlineExceeded`

The fix is to increase the `activeDeadlineSeconds` in the CronJob spec to allow more time for the export to complete.

input.note:
ROOT CAUSE: The ledger-export CronJob has an activeDeadlineSeconds limit of 3600 seconds (1 hour), but the job is taking approximately 2 hours to complete. The job is being terminated by Kubernetes when it reaches the deadline with status "DeadlineExceeded" [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/job#job-termination-and-cleanup-1].

EVIDENCE: Pod logs show the job started at 01:00:04Z and was killed at exactly 02:00:04Z (1 hour later) while processing batch 69/95 of the export. Previous successful runs completed before this issue appeared, suggesting the data volume has grown or performance has degraded.

FIX: Increase the activeDeadlineSeconds field in the ledger-export CronJob spec to a higher value (e.g., 7200 seconds for 2 hours, or higher if needed). This setting controls the maximum time allowed for a Job to run [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/job#job-termination-and-cleanup-1]. Update the CronJob manifest and redeploy it.
